root.claim: A deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: Build two faster tape procedures (address chunk interchange and simultaneous butterfly layers) from rank-saving linear networks, use them in synthetic polynomial transforms and resampled source transforms for a convolution, reduce integer multiplication to that convolution, then prove exactness and add up costs.

motivation.text: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, so savings are needed both in data movement and in arithmetic.

quote.quote: We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

children.method: Treat each fiber of $Q$ blocks as a list: split it at $Q-a$ into two pieces and merge them in the opposite order, which is a cyclic rotation of the blocks.
